question: What lets radiocarbon date the linseed oil in a modern forgery to within a few years?
answer: Fallout from nuclear tests. Bomb tests of the 1950s and early 1960s nearly doubled the carbon-14 in northern air, and it has fallen year by year since, so plants grown after 1955 carry a datable signature. In 2019 a speck of oil from a painting dated 1866 proved to come from flax harvested after 1958.
move: A disturbance that ruins one kind of record can become a clock for another.
reference: Laura Hendriks, Irka Hajdas et al., Uncovering modern paint forgeries by radiocarbon dating, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2019
